data.summary: The 16‑week plan spreads the 3‑hour weekly study load across all AP Physics 1 units, beginning with the student’s weak areas (Unit 6 and Unit 7) and revisiting them before the exam. Each week focuses on a small set of topic codes, includes concrete practice tasks, and builds toward two final review weeks (weeks 15‑16) that mix all topics and incorporate timed free‑response practice.

weeks.focus: Introduce rotating energy concepts and basic SHM definitions.
tasks: Read textbook sections 6.1 and 7.1; write a one‑page summary of key formulas.
Do 5 free‑response questions on rotational kinetic energy; check answers with the scoring guide.
Complete 5 conceptual questions on simple harmonic motion definitions.

weeks.focus: Deepen understanding of torque work and SHM frequency.
tasks: Watch a video on torque‑work relationships; solve 3 numerical problems.
Calculate frequency and period for 6 different pendulum setups.
Do 8 free‑response questions mixing torque‑work and SHM frequency; self‑grade.

weeks.focus: Angular momentum and SHM energy analysis.
tasks: Derive angular impulse equation; solve 4 practice problems.
Analyze 4 SHM graphs to determine amplitude, period, and phase.
Complete 6 FRQ parts that combine angular momentum with SHM energy.

weeks.focus: Conservation of angular momentum and SHM energy.
tasks: Solve 5 problems on conservation of angular momentum in collisions.
Calculate total energy at different points of a mass‑spring system for 5 cases.
Do a mixed set of 6 FRQs covering both topics; review scoring rubrics.
Work through 8 problems on rotational kinematics (θ, ω, α).
Convert 6 linear motion problems to rotational equivalents using 5.2.
Create a cheat sheet of key equations for Units 5 and 6.
Calculate torque for 5 different lever systems.
Determine rotational inertia for 4 common objects; compare with textbook values.
Do 6 FRQs that require both torque and inertia calculations.
Solve 7 problems on linear momentum and impulse.
Create flashcards for momentum‑related formulas.
Complete 5 free‑response items focusing on impulse concepts.

weeks.focus: Conservation of linear momentum and collisions.
tasks: Work through 6 elastic and 6 inelastic collision problems.
Write a one‑page explanation of when momentum is conserved.
Do 4 FRQs that integrate momentum conservation with energy ideas.
Calculate translational kinetic energy for 8 scenarios.
Solve 6 work‑by‑force problems; include sign conventions.
Determine potential energy for 5 gravitational and spring cases.
Complete 5 problems applying conservation of energy to roller‑coaster style questions.
Calculate power output for 4 real‑world machines.
Do a mixed set of 6 FRQs covering energy and power.
Draw free‑body diagrams for 6 different systems.
Solve 5 problems using Newton’s second law with multiple forces.
Create a summary sheet of common force vectors.
Work through 4 problems on action‑reaction pairs (2.3).
Solve 5 inertia‑related problems applying Newton’s first law.
Do 6 FRQs that require combining all three Newton’s laws.

weeks.focus: Kinematics in one and two dimensions.
tasks: Complete 8 velocity‑time and position‑time graph problems.
Solve 6 projectile motion questions using vector components.
Do 5 FRQs that integrate scalar‑vector distinctions with motion analysis.

weeks.focus: Reference frames and review of earlier units.
tasks: Explain relative motion in two reference frames; write a short paragraph.
Re‑solve one problem from each of Units 5, 6, 7 to reinforce connections.
Take a 20‑minute timed mini‑quiz covering weeks 1‑4 material.
Complete a full‑length 90‑minute practice FRQ set (all units).
Mark answers using the official scoring guide; note any recurring errors.
Review error log and rewrite one incorrect solution correctly.

weeks.focus: Final exam strategy and comprehensive review.
tasks: Take a timed 60‑minute multiple‑choice practice test.
Review every missed question; write a brief explanation of why the correct answer is right.
Create a one‑page cheat sheet of all key equations and concepts for quick last‑minute review.

data.final_week_advice: In the last two weeks, focus on timed practice, error analysis, and a concise formula sheet. Keep study sessions short (45 min) to maintain focus, and simulate exam conditions to build stamina. Rest well the night before the exam and trust the systematic preparation you’ve completed.
